findings.action: R2's guard still accepts a reader without an end-of-input check. Lines 111-112 accept any comparison with io.EOF, including a first-decode error check: dec.DisallowUnknownFields(); var v Config; if err := dec.Decode(&v); err != nil && err != io.EOF { return err }; return nil. That reader accepts a valid object followed by garbage or a second value, but strictJSONReaderEnds returns strict=true, ends=true. Lines 125-126 also accept errors.Is(err, io.EOF) even when its result is discarded. These are additional unlisted approximations beyond the spec's documented json.Unmarshal approximation. Associate the end condition with a read after the first value and require its non-EOF result to reject the input; add negative fixtures for first-decode EOF comparisons and ignored errors.Is results.
